It is utterly impossible that any one can enjoy solid happiness until he is possessed of the divine assurance that all his guilt has been canceled by the blood of the cross.

arxiv-1407-8076.title: Efficient formulation of the periodic corrections in Brouwer’s gravity solution Journal: Mathematical Problems in Engineering
arxiv-1407-8076.creator: Martin Lara
arxiv-1407-8076.description: Abstract The periodic terms of Brouwer’s gravity solution are reconstructed in a nonsingular set of variables which are derived from the well-known polar-nodal variables. This change does not affect the essence of the solution, which still keeps all the benefits of the action-angle variables approach, and yields two major improvements.

arxiv-2106-09278.title: Precision Higgs Measurements at the 250 GeV ILC
arxiv-2106-09278.description: Abstract The plan for the International Linear Collider (ILC) is now being prepared as a staged design, with the first stage of 2 ab − 1 {\rm ab^{-1}} at 250 GeV and later stages achieving the full project specifications with 4 ab − 1 {\rm ab^{-1}} at 500 GeV.

arxiv-2107-13005.title: Renormalization group improved implications of semileptonic operators in SMEFT
arxiv-2107-13005.description: Abstract We study implications of the four-fermion semileptonic operators at the low-energy and at electroweak (EW) scale in the framework of Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). We show how the renormalization group (RG) running effects can play an important role in probing the generic flavour structure of such operators.

arxiv-2201-06381.title: RF regulation with superconducting cavities and beam operation using a frequency shifted cavity
arxiv-2201-06381.creator: S. Pfeiffer, V. Ayvazyan, J. Branlard, T. Buettner, S. Choroba, B. Faatz, K. Honkavaara, V. Katalev, H. Schlarb, C. Schmidt, S. Schreiber, A. Sulimov, E. Vogel, H. Weise
arxiv-2201-06381.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by S. Pfeiffer, V. Ayvazyan, J. Branlard, T. Buettner, S. Choroba, B. Faatz, K. Honkavaara, V. Katalev, H. Schlarb, C. Schmidt, S. Schreiber, A. Sulimov, E. Vogel, H. Weise. The free-electron laser FLASH at DESY and the European XFEL are operated with superconducting radio frequency cavities and supply beam to several user experiments. The switching time between experiments is limited to dozens of microseconds.

arxiv-2202-08182.title: An Intrusion Response System utilizing Deep Q-Networks and System Partitions
arxiv-2202-08182.creator: Valeria Cardellini, Emiliano Casalicchio, Stefano Iannucci, Matteo Lucantonio, Sudip Mittal, Damodar Panigrahi, Andrea Silvi
arxiv-2202-08182.description: Abstract Intrusion Response is a relatively new field of research. Recent approaches for the creation of Intrusion Response Systems (IRSs) use Reinforcement Learning (RL) as a primary technique for the optimal or near-optimal selection of the proper countermeasure to take in order to stop or mitigate an ongoing attack.

arxiv-2203-03797.title: Learning Sensorimotor Primitives of Sequential Manipulation Tasks from Visual Demonstrations
arxiv-2203-03797.creator: Junchi Liang, Bowen Wen, Kostas Bekris, Abdeslam Boularias
arxiv-2203-03797.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Junchi Liang, Bowen Wen, Kostas Bekris, Abdeslam Boularias. This work aims to learn how to perform complex robot manipulation tasks that are composed of several, consecutively executed low-level sub-tasks, given as input a few visual demonstrations of the tasks performed by a person. The sub-tasks consist of moving the robot’s end-effector until it reaches a sub-goal region in the task space, performing an action, and triggering the next sub-task when a pre-condition is met.

arxiv-2301-10093.title: Polarization-Controlled Nonlinear Computer-Generated Holography
arxiv-2301-10093.creator: Lisa Ackermann, Clemens Roider, Kristian Cvecek, Nicolas Barré, Christian Aigner, Michael Schmidt
arxiv-2301-10093.description: Abstract Dynamic phase-only beam shaping with a liquid crystal spatial light modulator is a powerful technique for tailoring the intensity profile or wave front of a beam. While shaping and controlling the light field is a highly researched topic, dynamic nonlinear beam shaping has hardly been explored so far.

arxiv-2311-17239.title: Tail Risk and Systemic Risk Estimation of Cryptocurrencies: an Expectiles and Marginal Expected Shortfall based approach
arxiv-2311-17239.creator: Andrea Teruzzi
arxiv-2311-17239.description: Abstract This elaborate investigates the issue related to the quantification of the tail risk of cryptocurrencies. The statistical methods used in the study are those concerning recent developments of Extreme Value Theory (EVT) for weakly dependent data. This research proposes an expectile-based approach for the assessment of the tail risk of dependent data.

arxiv-2401-12377.title: ACS: Concurrent Kernel Execution on Irregular, Input-Dependent Computational Graphs
arxiv-2401-12377.creator: Sankeerth Durvasula 1 , Adrian Zhao 1 , Raymond Kiguru, Yushi Guan, Zhonghan Chen, Nandita Vijaykumar
arxiv-2401-12377.description: Abstract GPUs are widely used to accelerate many important classes of workloads today. However, in this work, we observe that several important emerging classes of workloads, including simulation engines for deep reinforcement learning and dynamic neural networks, are unable to fully utilize the massive parallelism that GPUs offer. These applications tend to have kernels that are small in size, i.e.

arxiv-2412-04929.title: Continuous Video Process: Modeling Videos as Continuous Multi-Dimensional Processes for Video Prediction
arxiv-2412-04929.creator: Gaurav Shrivastava, Abhinav Shrivastava
arxiv-2412-04929.description: Abstract Diffusion models have made significant strides in image generation, mastering tasks such as unconditional image synthesis, text-image translation, and image-to-image conversions. However, their capability falls short in the realm of video prediction, mainly because they treat videos as a collection of independent images, relying on external constraints such as temporal attention mechanisms to enforce temporal coherence.

arxiv-2412-19664.title: Non-reciprocal interactions preserve the universality class of Potts model
arxiv-2412-19664.creator: Soumya K. Saha and P. K. Mohanty
arxiv-2412-19664.description: Abstract We study the q q -state Potts model on a square lattice with directed nearest-neighbor spin-spin interactions that are inherently non-reciprocal. Both equilibrium and non-equilibrium dynamics are investigated. Analytically, we demonstrate that non-reciprocal interactions do not alter the critical exponents of the model under equilibrium dynamics. In contrast, numerical simulations with selfish non-equilibrium dynamics reveal distinctive behavior.

arxiv-2501-04537.description: Abstract . Two classic results, due to K. Doerk and P. Hall respectively, establish the solvability of those finite groups all of whose maximal subgroups are supersolvable, and the solvability of finite groups in which all maximal subgroups have prime or squared prime index.

arxiv-2503-05688.title: Boundary stratifications of Hurwitz spaces
arxiv-2503-05688.creator: Darragh Glynn
arxiv-2503-05688.description: Abstract . Let ℋ \mathcal{H} be a Hurwitz space that parametrises holomorphic maps to ℙ 1 \mathbb{P}^{1} . Abramovich, Corti and Vistoli, building on work of Harris and Mumford, describe a compactification ℋ ¯ \overline{\mathcal{H}} with a natural boundary stratification.

arxiv-2504-11314.title: Second Law of Black Holes Thermodynamics in Non-Quasi-Static Processes
arxiv-2504-11314.description: Abstract The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy satisfies the generalized second law of black hole thermodynamics for arbitrary thermodynamic evolution within Einstein-Maxwell theory. In contrast, the black hole entropy that satisfies the second law in low-energy effective modified gravity theories related to quantum gravity is derived solely by considering linear perturbations within quasi-static processes.

arxiv-2504-16232.title: On evolutionary equations related to skew-symmetric spatial operators
arxiv-2504-16232.creator: Evgeny Yu. Panov
arxiv-2504-16232.description: Abstract We study generalized solutions of an evolutionary equation related to some densely defined skew-symmetric operator in a real Hilbert space. We establish existence of a contractive semigroup, which provides generalized solutions, and suggest a criteria of uniqueness of this semigroup. We also find a stronger criteria of uniqueness of generalized solutions.

pmc-10540404.title: Neuronal MHC-I complex is destabilized by amyloid-β and its implications in Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-10540404.creator: Min-Seok Kim, Kwangmin Cho, Mi-Hyang Cho, Na-Young Kim, Kyunggon Kim, Dong-Hou Kim, Seung-Yong Yoon
pmc-10540404.description: BackgroundsThe expression of major histocompatibility complex I (MHC-I) in neurons has recently been shown to regulate neurite outgrowth and synaptic plasticity. However, its contribution to neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains largely unknown.MethodsIn this study, we investigated the relationship between impaired MHC-I-β2M complex and AD in vitro and human AD samples.

pmc-10587913.title: Huge Antrochoanal Polyp: A Case Report
pmc-10587913.creator: Salmah M Alharbi, Anas M Alshehri, Ibrahem H Erwe
pmc-10587913.description: Antrochoanal polyps are benign lesions arising from the maxillary sinus mucosa. The most common patient complaint is unilateral nasal obstruction. Nasal endoscopy and computed tomography are the gold standard modalities for diagnosis. Treatment is surgical. We report the case of a 19-year-old female suffering from a huge antrochoanal polyp who went to hospital following a choking episode.

pmc-10724699.title: Lobar Mucus Plugging Reflecting Central Bronchial Tumoral Obstruction: A Case Report
pmc-10724699.creator: Asma Bensliman, Denis Tack
pmc-10724699.description: Early diagnosis of bronchopulmonary carcinoid tumors is crucial as the surgical excision is the main treatment and determines the prognosis. We present the case of a 66-year-old heavy-smoker man who had started to complain about a cough a few months ago.

pmc-11285955.title: Evaluating Doppel’s impact on Anxiety and Focus amongst adults with ADHD
pmc-11285955.creator: Georgina Bartlett, Daniel Frings, Eddie Chaplin, Mengling Feng, Daniel B. Forger
pmc-11285955.description: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is the most commonly diagnosed psychiatric disorder in children. Amongst adults, it is often underdiagnosed and associated with comorbidities including anxiety. This study presents a trial evaluating the efficacy of Doppel, a wrist-worn wearable that provides vibrations linked to one’s heart rate to improve symptoms of anxiety and poor focus amongst young adults with ADHD.

pmc-11484460.title: Enhancement of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) with guanidine hydrochloride for the detection of Streptococcus equi subspecies equi (Strangles)
pmc-11484460.creator: Alexandra Knox, Travis Beddoe
pmc-11484460.description: Streptococcus equi subspecies equi, commonly referred to as “strangles”, poses a significant biosecurity challenge across equine farms worldwide. The continuous prevalence and highly transmissibility of strangles necessitates a rapid and accurate diagnostic procedure. However, current “gold-standard” techniques, such as cultures and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), are unreliable or inaccessible, and require lengthy periods between sample collection and results.

pmc-11536541.title: Molecular analysis of vector-borne pathogens in Eurasian badgers (Meles meles) from continental Europe
pmc-11536541.creator: Zoë Tess Lara Lindhorst, Sebastian Brandstetter, Maria Sophia Unterköfler, Barbara Eigner, Joachim Spergser, Marc Colyn, Peter Steinbach, Duško Ćirović, Nikica Šprem, Tomislav Dumić, Vincenzo Veneziano, Franz Müller, Josef Harl, Georgiana Deak, Angela Monica Ionică, Mike Heddergott, Hans-Peter Fuehr
pmc-11536541.description: BackgroundVector-borne pathogens (VBPs) are increasing in significance in veterinary medicine and public health settings, with wildlife playing a potentially crucial role in their transmission. Eurasian badgers (Meles meles) are widely distributed across Europe. However, information currently available on the prevalence of VBPs in badgers is limited.

pmc-12750870.title: The role of indocyanine green in the intraoperative navigation of gastric cancer surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12750870.creator: Nassuf Mourdi, Yongke Wu, Yuanhao Su, Yiyuan Zhao, Xin Jin, Yunhao Li, Zhidong Wang
pmc-12750870.description: ObjectiveIndocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence imaging is increasingly being recognized as promising technique for guiding surgical procedures in gastric cancer treatment. Nevertheless, current meta-analyses have not yet fully explored its impact on lymph node (LN) dissection or evaluated its effectiveness across open, laparoscopic, and robotic surgical techniques.

pmc-12855991.title: Monitoring strain evolution in water-sand systems using distributed acoustic sensing for geohazard early warning
pmc-12855991.creator: Yingping Li, Min Sun, Yingcai Zheng, David Li, Lianjie Huang
pmc-12855991.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Rainfall-driven hazards such as landslides, debris flows, and earthen dam failures often arise when water changes the internal strain within sand. This study evaluates the ability of distributed acoustic sensing to monitor these strain changes in real time. We embed a fiber-optic cable in a sand-filled glass cylinder and run controlled dry- and wet-sand experiments to measure how strain develops as water infiltrates, saturates, and drains from the sand.

pmc-12931617.title: Procedural outcome and safety of percutaneous patent ductus arteriosus occlusion in adults
pmc-12931617.creator: Abdul Malik Sheikh, Asma Kanwal, Hina Sattar, Tauqeer Akbar, Syed Najam Hyder, Tayyaba Saher
pmc-12931617.description: Background:Percutaneous device closure of patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in infants and children is a frequently performed procedure. However, transcatheter closure is rare in adults, especially in developed countries, as most ducts are typically closed in childhood. PDA in adults poses unique challenges due to age-related comorbidities and some morphological changes in PDA that occur with advanced age.

pmc-13242615.title: Back to Basics: Daily Saline Wet Dressings as a Turning Point in Recurrent Pediatric Split-Thickness Skin Graft Failure
pmc-13242615.creator: Jana H Mahdi, Elie Moukawam, Ziad R Hankach, George Ghanime, Ziad Sleiman
pmc-13242615.description: Split-thickness skin grafting (STSG) is a widely used reconstructive technique for managing traumatic soft tissue defects. Successful graft take depends on adequate wound bed preparation and effective infection control. Multidrug-resistant infections remain a major cause of graft failure, particularly in complex pediatric trauma cases.
